newsitem.title: POLAND: FAST-TRACK FINES FOR SOCCER THUGS IN POLAND.
newsitem.headline: FAST-TRACK FINES FOR SOCCER THUGS IN POLAND.

text.p: Poland has arranged for courts to hand down instant sentences for football hooligans during a weekend World Cup qualifying match against Moldova in the southern city of Katowice, the PAP news agency said on Friday.
Justice Minister Leszek Kubicki was reported to have granted a request by Katowice's governor to temporarily introduce the fast-track penalties on Saturday and Sunday, after first refusing.
The police will whisk hooligans in front of magistrates the moment they are caught disturbing the peace, destroying property, carrying dangerous objects or setting off fireworks.
PAP said the minister had granted permission after the governor sent an account of battles among fans at a recent ice-hockey match and a general rise in violence at local sports events.
"In changing his mind, the minister recognised that there was a justified reasons for introducing a rapid sentencing procedure," Kubicki's spokeswoman Barbara Makosa-Stepkowska told the agency.
Poland has started cracking down on soccer hooliganism following a spate of incidents, shutting one major stadium until next year and installing video cameras at others.
